title: British Tamils protest in London over removal of Thileepan statue
seoTitle: London protest over Thileepan statue removal

tea.why: The removal of a statue of LTTE hunger striker Thileepan from the Nallur area in northern Sri Lanka.
tea.want: To protest the removal of the statue and express support for Thileepan's legacy.
tea.changed: Oct 9: The British High Commission in Colombo declined to comment on the display of banned LTTE flags during the London protest.

summary: Members of the Sri Lankan Tamil diaspora in the United Kingdom held a demonstration in London. The protest was organized in response to the removal of a statue of Thileepan, a senior political wing leader of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) who died during a hunger strike in 1987 in Jaffna, Sri Lanka. During the event, participants displayed LTTE flags, which drew attention due to the organization's banned status under the UK's Terrorism Act 2000. When questioned about the display of these symbols, the British High Commission in Colombo declined to provide a direct response, reiterating its standard position. No official clarification was reported from UK law enforcement agencies.
demands: Protest the removal of the Thileepan statue in Jaffna
response: The British High Commission in Colombo declined to directly address questions regarding the display of banned LTTE flags, reiterating its standard position. No official clarification was reported from UK law enforcement agencies.

updates.text: The British High Commission in Colombo declined to comment on the display of banned LTTE flags during the London protest.
